label: late original-phase c/r/3/f/t/d/a/e after several 2/0/n/w/g/q-type tokens
explanation: Fires almost only during the original (input) phase (99% of mass), at positions 3-8 (never at t<2), with a weak tail on the <DEL> step and never in the copy phase. The current input token matters most: c, r, 3, f, then t, d, a, e (lift 2-6x), usually on its first occurrence. Activity grows with how many tokens from a second set (2, 0, n, w, g, q, l, h, b, u) have already appeared earlier in the sequence; the top examples start with 2/0 followed by several of these. Earlier occurrences of the c/r/f-type tokens seem to lower it. This looks like a graded, roughly additive mix of the current token and accumulated history, so boolean thresholds plateau around dev F1 0.44-0.46. Recall and precision are both clearly incomplete. Magnitude rises with the count of 2/0/n/w-type tokens already seen (checked: precision goes from 0.24 at >=2 to 0.54 at >=4). It does not fire on x, j, y or most other letters as input, or on any copy-phase step.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=3: c, r, 3, f; t=4: c, r, f, 3; t=6: c, r, f, 3) and the first original token (most: 2, 0, n, w, g, q; least: d, c, 3, r); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=4, t=6.
